The main difference is that tsx transpiles with esbuild and does not type-check, while ts-node uses the TypeScript compiler and type-checks by default unless you run it in transpile-only mode. tsx also hooks Node's module loading so ESM and CJS TypeScript files work together without extra flags, which is usually the pain point with ts-node. The trade-off is that type errors only show up if you run `tsc --noEmit` separately. Also, the lockfile from the tsx addition in packages/cli still hasn't been updated.
Action: Run the install from the repo root to refresh the lockfile, if you tell me which command you use, and keep `tsc --noEmit` as the type check.

Most likely the htmx request from the partial isn't carrying the CSRF token: Django needs it either as a hidden `csrfmiddlewaretoken` field in the posted form or in the `X-CSRFToken` header, and a token that only sits in the base template isn't sent with requests from inside the partial. The usual fixes are putting `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form in the partial, or setting `hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}'` on `<body>` in the base template so every htmx request gets it. I'd also confirm the CSRF cookie is actually set on that page.
Action: Ask you to paste the partial and the base template's body tag (or point me at them) so I can see which of these applies, then make the change.

That pattern fits rounding once on the fractional total while each line is shown rounded. Unit prices are integer cents and quantities can be fractional (like 2.5 hours), so each line should be rounded to whole cents first and then summed. Display should go through formatMoney(cents, currency) rather than dividing by 100 by hand. I haven't looked at the code yet, so this is the probable cause.
